cards.title: Spoon Ferry Crumb-Light Opening
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only pencil cup opening card for a fictional lunchbox harbor start with one setting clue: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: place a pencil cup or drawn cup nearby and ask for one invented harbor detail only: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Kid: start the story by noticing where the spoon ferry waits in the pretend harbor: ____________________.
cards.firstLinePrompt: First line: On the edge of Lunchbox Harbor, the spoon ferry waited beside ____________________.
cards.characterPrompt: Character arrival: A helper arrives carrying ____________________.
cards.placePrompt: Place doorway: The first doorway into the story is a cracker dock, napkin pier, or lunchbox lid gate called ____________________.
cards.objectPrompt: Object invitation: Pick one tiny object that invites the story to begin: ____________________.
cards.questionPrompt: Opening question: What clue makes the harbor feel different today? ____________________.
cards.nextMovePrompt: Next move: The helper's first gentle action is to ____________________.
cards.reviseOpeningPrompt: Revise opening: Add one setting clue the reader can see, hear, or touch: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only the harbor object and one describing word: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A setting clue can open a pretend spoon ferry story: ____________________.

cards.title: Acorn Desk First Errand Bell
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only pencil cup opening card for a fictional acorn errand-office story that starts with a clear task: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: set this card beside a pencil cup sketch and invite one made-up errand, not real chores or real details: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Kid: begin when the acorn desk gives the helper one small job for the story: ____________________.
cards.firstLinePrompt: First line: The acorn desk bell rang because the tiniest errand slip said ____________________.
cards.characterPrompt: Character arrival: A leaf-list clerk, button-badge helper, or invented visitor steps in to ____________________.
cards.placePrompt: Place doorway: The story opens at the acorn counter where ____________________.
cards.objectPrompt: Object invitation: The first object from the pencil cup becomes a walnut stamp, twig pen, or ____________________.
cards.questionPrompt: Opening question: Which task needs help before the office can settle down? ____________________.
cards.nextMovePrompt: Next move: The helper reads the slip, chooses one desk corner, and ____________________.
cards.reviseOpeningPrompt: Revise opening: Underline the task word and make it clearer or stranger: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Circle one task object and finish one short sentence: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A task hook gives the first paragraph a job to follow: ____________________.

cards.title: Seed Drawer Foldout Beginning
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only pencil cup opening card for a fictional seed-library story that begins when a folded map appears on paper: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: invite a made-up map on the page and avoid narrow real-world place details: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Kid: start with one map symbol that changes how the seed library feels: ____________________.
cards.firstLinePrompt: First line: When the drawer opened, a folded seed map showed ____________________.
cards.characterPrompt: Character arrival: The map keeper arrives with a catalog card asking for ____________________.
cards.placePrompt: Place doorway: The story enters through a drawer aisle, map table, or paper seed arch named ____________________.
cards.objectPrompt: Object invitation: Choose the map object that begins the tale, such as a seed bead, ruler ribbon, paper key, or ____________________.
cards.questionPrompt: Opening question: Which invented map mark should the hero trust first? ____________________.
cards.nextMovePrompt: Next move: The hero studies one border, one symbol, and then ____________________.
cards.reviseOpeningPrompt: Revise opening: Add a map clue that points to a fictional place, not a real one: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Draw one symbol and write its invented meaning here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A map start can make the first scene feel ready to explore on paper: ____________________.

cards.title: Rain Gauge Platform Silver Signal
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only pencil cup opening card for a fictional rain-gauge railway start with one pretend weather signal: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: set a pencil cup or drawn cup beside the page and ask for invented weather, not real forecasts or plans: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Kid: begin the railway story when the gauge shows a signal no one expected: ____________________.
cards.firstLinePrompt: First line: At Rain Gauge Railway, the silver gauge tipped toward ____________________.
cards.characterPrompt: Character arrival: A rain-note conductor, cloud-sample sorter, or garden forecast writer arrives holding ____________________.
cards.placePrompt: Place doorway: The first scene begins at a platform, gauge shed, or puddle bridge called ____________________.
cards.objectPrompt: Object invitation: Pick a weather object that invites the story to start, such as a blue ticket, clear tube, cloud note, or ____________________.
cards.questionPrompt: Opening question: What does the pretend weather signal seem to ask? ____________________.
cards.nextMovePrompt: Next move: The hero checks the gauge mark, listens to the platform bell, and ____________________.
cards.reviseOpeningPrompt: Revise opening: Add one weather signal before explaining what anyone does: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Mark the gauge level and write one signal word: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A weather signal can pull the reader into a fictional railway opening: ____________________.

cards.title: Moss Observatory Lantern Note
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only pencil cup opening card for a fictional moss observatory story that begins with a gentle mystery note: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: place the card with paper and invite only invented moss signals, sky marks, and note words: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Kid: begin when a moss note appears where the observer did not expect it: ____________________.
cards.firstLinePrompt: First line: The moss message on the observatory shelf read ____________________.
cards.characterPrompt: Character arrival: A careful observer, pebble-lens keeper, or invented visitor arrives to ____________________.
cards.placePrompt: Place doorway: The first doorway is a lookout step, lantern shelf, or moss arch named ____________________.
cards.objectPrompt: Object invitation: Choose the object that carries the note, such as a moss dial, pebble lens, folded sky chart, or ____________________.
cards.questionPrompt: Opening question: Why would the moss leave this message today? ____________________.
cards.nextMovePrompt: Next move: The observer copies the note onto paper and then ____________________.
cards.reviseOpeningPrompt: Revise opening: Make the note more specific by adding one color, shape, or soft sound: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write the note's first two words and stop there: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A gentle mystery note can start a pretend observatory story: ____________________.
